newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. stock index futures finish higher.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. stock index futures finish higher.

text.p: Most U.S. stock index futures finished higher and could continue to rise into the triple-witching expiration on Friday, traders said.
"We will continue to be firm into the end of the week," Daniel Riley, director of institutional trading at Chicago Execution Corp, said.
Many traders are expecting an uneventful expiration after several weeks of extremely volatile markets. They said dealers and institutions were already positioned ahead of expiration.
Wednesday's session was described as the slowest in two weeks.
March Standard & Poor's 500s could rise to 742.00 to 743.00, and possibly press into the 752.00 area before Christmas, Riley and other traders said.

Riley said S&Ps could rally sharply on the last two days of the year if the buying spree in technology stocks continues. Optimism about holiday PC sales and year-end book-squaring sparked heavy buying in blue-chip technology stocks on Wednesday.
The technology-rich Nasdaq composite rose 1.5 percent, contributing to the S&P market's resiliency in the face of weakening U.S. bond prices.

U.S. bond prices fell on technical factors, as well as the softer than expected two-year bond auction, traders said. The decline in bond prices nudged U.S. interest rates slightly higher but had little effect on the overall U.S. stock market.
Traders said estimated volume for March S&Ps was at about 80,000 contracts. Aside from heavy buying from several large U.S. firms and one notable fund manager, trades were spotty.
"There is little to no local activity," one trader said. "A lot of locals left for the year. They've taken a hit and don't want to risk anything more."

March S&Ps closed slightly under fair value, which currently stands at 6.80 points to cash. There were no arbitrage buy or sell programs reported. Arbitrage buy programs were expected at about a 7.80 point premium to cash and arbitrage sell programs at a premium of 5.80 points, traders said.

At the end of pit trade, March S&Ps were up 4.90 at 738.15, New Composites were up 2.00 at 388.45, Value Lines were 3.90 higher at 677.40, Nikkeis were off 260.0 at 20,130, Midcap 400s were 2.20 higher at 252.60 and Nasdaq 100s were up 24.25 at 849.75.
